children: Life360's bull at Bell Potter says the 15% share-price fall that followed the location-app developer's 3Q result yesterday seems to be due to some disappointment in advertising revenue in the near term. "In our view this is more than offset by the strength in subscription revenue," analyst Chris Savage says. A price rise in the U.S. of $2/month for Gold membership should help to drive continued strong subscription revenue growth in 2027, Bell Potter says. Gold membership represents some 84% of paying circles. It keeps a buy call on Life360, which is up 7.8% at A$20.38 today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
